briefing.headline: Kestrel’s press and high turnovers couldn’t stop Harbour’s central threat; Harbour extended control after the break

first_half.text: Harbour consistently attacked through the centre and converted that threat into goals (two in the first half).
Kestrel pressed high and recovered balls often but could not turn that into scores, arriving in the final third more frequently without scoring.

changes.text: Harbour shifted more activity into the centre and left after the break: centre entries rose from 1.11 to 1.22 per_window and left entries from 0.67 to 1 per_window.
Kestrel’s pressing eased in the second half: their PPDA rose from 4.9 to 5.9 (per five-minute-window average), reflecting less aggressive pressing.

Harbour increased final-third activity and possession in the attacking third after the break, with final-third entries rising from 2.33 to 3.11 per_window and final-third possession from 51.5% to 64.7%.

predictions.text: Gregor Molina would try to force Harbour wider by crowding midfield, reducing Harbour’s central entries.
Kestrel’s press would ease and PPDA would rise (4.9 -> 5.9 per_window).
Kestrel would push to increase final-third entries substantially; their entries rose only from 3.56 to 3.67 per_window.
Harbour would markedly increase progressive passes to punish spaces; the progressive-pass signal did not show the predicted jump.
Harbour would increase final-third entries to keep Kestrel under pressure; entries rose from 2.33 to 3.11 per_window.

result.text: Harbour converted central and final-third control into three goals across the match (two in the first half, one in the second).
Kestrel’s early pressing and high turnovers produced recoveries but no goals; they kept similar shot volumes across the game yet finished with zero goals.
The half-time swing—Kestrel easing their press while Harbour increased central and left-channel entries and final-third possession—explains Harbour’s control and the 0-3 final score.
